mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation/Company Registration Certificate of the Taiwan investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Administration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Non-Hague consular legalization route because Taiwan is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention: obtain the certified original from MOEA; submit it to the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) for certification; SEF forwards a duplicate to the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) for verification; use the ARATS-verified duplicate for PRC SAMR, tax, and bank filings. Do not chain with a Hague Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Equivalent Company Registration Extract issued by the Taiwan competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) or the applicable Taiwan District Court registration office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Non-Hague consular legalization route: obtain the official certificate; submit to SEF for certification; ARATS verification; then acceptance by PRC authorities. No Hague Apostille is permitted because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Taiwan investor approving the establishment of the PRC WFOE, capital contribution amount, and appointment of legal representative and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwan investing company, with signatures notarized by a Taiwan notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Taiwan before an authorized notary public; certification by SEF; verification by ARATS; submission to the PRC registration authority. This is the standalone non-Hague consular legalization equivalent and must not be combined with apostille certification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of the Taiwan investing entity (consolidated and certified as current)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) certified copy of the investor's articles of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: MOEA certified copy followed by SEF certification and ARATS verification, then inclusion in the PRC incorporation file. The ARATS/SEF route replaces consular legalization; Hague Apostille does not apply.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Taiwan investor's primary bank confirming account history, relationship length, and absence of adverse AML flags
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan depositary bank or financial institution where the investor maintains its main operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank signatory executes the letter before a Taiwan notary public; the notarized bank letter is certified by SEF and verified by ARATS before presentation to the PRC bank and SAMR. This route is not a Hague Apostille and cannot be chained with one.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the Taiwan investor, all UBOs, directors, managers, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of Taiwan (R.O.C.), consolidated text effective 2021, Chapter II (Limited Company), Articles 98 through 118; Chapter VII (Foreign Companies), Articles 370 through 387; Article 387 (Company Registration Filing); Foreign Investment Act, Articles 4, 6, 7, 10 and 14; Enforcement Rules of the Foreign Investment Act; Company Registration Rules promulgated by the Ministry of Economic Affairs
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company Registration and Commercial Administration Division, acting jointly with the MOEA Investment Commission for foreign investment approval and the One-Stop Company Registration Service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application (Limited Liability Company / Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise) filed under Article 387 of the Companies Act and the MOEA Company Registration Rules, together with the approved Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Taiwan Companies Act for a limited liability company. However, for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise, the foreign investor must subscribe and pay the initial capital into a Taiwan bank account before the incorporation application is submitted, with a Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate and a bank balance/passbook certificate used as capital verification evidence. No blocked escrow account is required for an ordinary non-regulated wholesale trading company, but the MOEA Investment Commission reviews whether the proposed paid-up capital is reasonably commensurate with the declared business scope, projected turnover, operating costs and working capital needs.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN_WFOE_LTD (THE COMPANY), TAIWAN. THE UNDERSIGNED, being all of the directors/shareholders of the Company, acting by unanimous written consent in accordance with the Companies Act of Taiwan and the Articles of Incorporation, and without the necessity of a physical meeting, hereby adopt and confirm the following resolutions as of the date of execution, with such resolutions to be effective immediately and to be filed in the Company corporate minute book. WHEREAS the Company is a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise within the meaning of the Foreign Investment Act, incorporated as a limited liability company under the Companies Act of Taiwan; and WHEREAS the authorized capital of the Company and the initial subscribed capital have been determined in the Articles of Incorporation, and the business scope includes wholesale distribution and ocean vessel freight logistics of Portland cement clinker, hydraulic cement and related construction materials; and WHEREAS the first board is empowered to establish the initial operational infrastructure of the Company, including the subscription and payment of share capital, the opening of bank accounts, the adoption of a registered office, and the appointment of statutory officers. NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS. FIRST, SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The initial paid-up share capital of the Company is hereby fixed in the amount of [US$1,000,000] or its New Taiwan Dollar equivalent, divided into shares of par value [NT$10] each. The shareholder has fully subscribed to all such shares and the directors are directed to procure that the entire subscription proceeds are remitted from abroad in freely convertible foreign currency into a Taiwan designated foreign exchange bank account, and that a capital verification certificate and foreign exchange remittance certificate be delivered to the Ministry of Economic Affairs with the incorporation registration documents. No share certificate, register entry or dividend right shall be issued until full payment of the subscribed capital is actually received and recorded in the Company books. SECOND, BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The board hereby authorizes the opening and maintenance of all corporate bank accounts, including foreign currency, New Taiwan Dollar, demand deposit and custody accounts, at [Bank and Branch]. The President, Chief Financial Officer, and any two of the directors designated by the President are authorized to sign account documentation, endorse and issue cheques and payment instruments, execute electronic fund transfers and foreign exchange contracts, and act as authorized bank signatories in a manner consistent with the bank mandate. For any payment exceeding [NT$500,000], dual signatures of two authorized officers shall be required. THIRD, REGISTERED OFFICE. The board hereby adopts [Address, Taipei, Taiwan] as the registered office of the Company, the street address and actual physical location of which shall be filed with the MOEA Department of Commerce. The Company Secretary is authorized to execute any lease, landlord consent, registered office consent or building use declaration, and to submit all necessary filings to the competent municipal authority so that the Company possesses a lawful and serviceable address for the receipt of legal process and official notices. FOURTH, APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The following persons are appointed, effective immediately, as statutory officers of the Company: [President], [Chief Financial Officer], and [Company Secretary]. The Company Secretary is expressly authorized to sign, certify, notarize and file the Articles of Incorporation, board resolutions, registration applications, tax registrations, customs registrations, bank mandates and any other documents required under applicable law to complete the statutory incorporation of the Company and to commence operations. This resolution is final, valid and binding on the Company and its organs, and the minute book shall reflect its adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Step 1 - Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA-IC), online via the MOEA Company and Economic Development One-Stop Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a foreign investment application under the Foreign Investment Act using the MOEA-IC online forms. Attach a duly notarized certificate of corporate existence of the foreign parent, proof of authorized signatory powers, proposed Articles of Incorporation, a business plan and financial forecast reflecting the purpose of wholesale distribution of Portland cement clinker and hydraulic cement, and a bank reference letter confirming the investor financial capacity. The MOEA-IC will review sector eligibility, national security considerations, capital adequacy and the proposed corporate structure. In parallel, submit a company name reservation application for both the English and Chinese names to the MOEA One-Stop Service. The name reservation and foreign investment approval are prerequisite pre-filing conditions for the formal company registration.
required_dossiers: MOEA-IC Foreign Investment Application Form
Notarized certificate of incorporation of the ultimate foreign investor
Certificate of authorized signatory and board authority
Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Business scope and implementation plan
Bank reference and source of funds evidence
Company name reservation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, file a written response to the MOEA-IC within 14 days, correcting or clarifying the cited deficiency by amending the proposed business scope or capital allocation. If the suspension is not lifted, request an administrative review under the Administrative Procedure Act, or submit a fresh application after curing the defect without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Step 2 - Capital Subscription, Notarization and Paid-Up Capital Arrangement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan District Court Notary Public or licensed notary public, in coordination with a Central Bank of Taiwan designated foreign exchange bank (DBU/OBU)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the MOEA-IC approval letter, finalize the Articles of Incorporation and obtain notarization of the subscriber and director signatures. The foreign parent must execute a capital subscription undertaking and wire the entire initial paid-up capital into a temporary or newly opened corporate bank account in Taiwan. The designated foreign exchange bank will issue a Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate and a Deposit Balance Certificate, which together form the capital verification evidence required for registration. If the company premises lease is ready, the lease or landlord consent should also be notarized. All executed documents, including the board resolution, Articles of Incorporation and identity documents, must be presented to the notary with original passport or corporate seal evidence and certified translations as needed.
required_dossiers: MOEA-IC foreign investment approval letter
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Shareholder capital subscription undertaking
Designated foreign exchange bank remittance certificate
Bank statement or deposit balance certificate
Certified passport/company registration extract of the foreign investor
Control certificate of registered office or landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign exchange remittance is rejected by the bank due to AML or source of funds queries, provide updated corporate structure charts, audited financial statements and transaction records to the bank compliance team. If notarization is rejected due to defective documents, correct, re-execute and re-notarize the instruments before proceeding to registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Step 3 - Company Incorporation Registration with MOEA Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce - Company Registration Division and One-Stop Company Registration Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Company Establishment Registration Application electronically with the MOEA One-Stop Portal. The application must attach a certified copy of the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the board resolution, the capital verification certificate, the registered office consent, and the identity documents of directors and statutory officers. The Department of Commerce will examine the company name, business scope, capital subscription, legality of the objects under the Company Act, registered office address and the appointment of legal representatives. If the filing package is complete and no substantive legal objection exists, the MOEA will issue the Company Registration Certificate and assign the statutory Unified Business Number, which is the foundation for subsequent tax, customs, social insurance and licensing registrations.
required_dossiers: Company Establishment Registration Application Form
Certified or notarized Articles of Incorporation
First Board Resolution and incorporation-related shareholder resolutions
Capital verification certificate including bank foreign exchange documents
Registered office consent or lease
Identification documents of directors and statutory officers
Company seal or chop registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, cure all deficiencies within 15 calendar days by filing supplementary evidence or replacement documents. If the application is rejected, file an administrative appeal within the statutory period and resubmit a complete application with all identified legal defects rectified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Step 4 - Tax, Customs, Social Insurance and Operational Post-Registration Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance, local municipal tax office, Directorate General of Customs for import/export registration, and the Bureau of Labor Insurance and Occupational Safety and Health Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after receiving the MOEA company registration certificate, file the Business Tax Registration and Income Tax Registration with the relevant National Taxation Bureau using the Unified Business Number. Obtain the company Uniform Invoice Seal and register the VAT obligations under the Business Tax Act. If the WFOE will import cement clinker or export cement products, register with the Directorate General of Customs and obtain the customs import/export code. The company should also register with the Labor Insurance Bureau, National Health Insurance Administration and labor pension system for all employees. For any physical warehouse, storage silo, packing or reloading facility used in the wholesale operations, the company must obtain the trade and warehouse operating permit described in the industrial licensing section and provide fire safety, structural and environmental compliance documents to the local municipal authority.
required_dossiers: MOEA Company Registration Certificate
Unified Business Number and tax registration application
Uniform Invoice Seal registration form
Lease or ownership proof for office and warehouse premises
Bank account confirmation and foreign exchange registrations
Customs registration application if importing or exporting
Employee roster and labor insurance/NHI registration forms
Fire safety and building occupancy certificate for any physical facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is queried, respond with corrected forms and supporting evidence to the National Taxation Bureau within the notice period. If customs registration is suspended, petition the Directorate General of Customs with the import/export code and any missing customs reporting documents. If labor insurance or tax penalties arise, submit the required declarations, pay any administrative fines if applicable, and request a formal reconsideration under the respective tax or labor procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Bureau, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA); local municipal Department of Economic Development; Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration (EPA); National Fire Agency, Ministry of the Interior; and Occupational Safety and Health Administration, Ministry of Labor
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Registration for Wholesale of Construction Materials and General Warehouse Operating Permit for Non-Manufacturing Storage of Portland Cement Clinker and Hydraulic Cement

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan (Taiwan EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Environmental Registration / Exempt from Full EIA for a pure wholesale and enclosed storage operation; no full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is mandated provided the facility is not located in a sensitive environmental zone and total cementitious material storage capacity remains below the thresholds set by the EPA. If storage capacity or transshipment intensity exceeds the applicable threshold, a Light Environmental Impact Assessment or a statutorily prescribed environmental impact report will be required prior to construction or operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater is expected to be generated by the wholesale distribution and covered storage of cement clinker. If any silo washout stormwater or floor drain discharge is produced, comply with effluent limits of pH 6 to 9, total suspended solids below 50 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand below 100 mg/L, and biochemical oxygen demand below 30 mg/L. Ambient particulate matter at the facility boundary must not exceed 150 micrograms per cubic meter for PM10 on a 24-hour basis and 35 micrograms per cubic meter for PM2.5 on a 24-hour basis. If a particulate control or baghouse system is installed for cement dust, such stack emissions shall not exceed 100 mg/Nm3 of total particulate in general zones, with stricter standards of 80 mg/Nm3 if the facility is located in a high-density urban area. VOCs are not expected from cement clinker storage; any incidental solvent or lubricant use shall not exceed the Taiwan stationary source VOC reporting threshold of 0.6 tonnes per year. Hazardous waste, including contaminated filtering media or used lubricating oil, shall be stored separately, manifested under the waste disposal code system, and delivered only to licensed waste carriers.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The facility shall obtain a Fire Safety Compliance Certificate from the local Fire Department under the Fire Services Act, including an approved fire protection plan, emergency escape routes, fire extinguishers and automatic alarm system where the floor area exceeds the statutory threshold. A structural load inspection certificate must be issued by a registered professional civil engineer confirming that the warehouse floor, silo foundations and racking systems are capable of supporting the intended clinker and cement loads. Work site inspections under the Occupational Safety and Health Act must verify dust control measures, personal protective equipment, equipment safe operating distances, material stacking stability, proper housekeeping and the provision of a workplace emergency evacuation plan. If mechanical conveyors, forklifts or cranes are used, each unit must have the required inspection certificate, and the site shall employ a designated safety officer with the appropriate Taiwan occupational training certification before bulk operations commence.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online filing through the National Unified Electronic Tax Bureau (E-Tax Bureau) platform accessible via www.chinatax.gov.cn and, for VAT invoicing, the STA National Electronic Invoice Service Platform
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The PRC-incorporated WFOE obtains a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) from the State Administration for Market Regulation at incorporation; the USCC is the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) for all PRC taxes. Within 30 days of business license issuance, the WFOE must complete initial tax registration with its competent county-level STA tax bureau through the E-Tax Bureau portal or in-person counter, submitting the SAMR business license, articles of association, legal representative identification, registered address proof, bank account details, and appointed tax administrator information. After registration, the tax bureau records the taxpayer, applies the entity-level corporate income tax classification and VAT status, and activates the electronic invoice and tax-control account. Foreign non-resident shareholders do not obtain a separate Chinese TIN solely as equity holders; a non-resident enterprise earning Chinese-source income without a permanent establishment is handled through the WFOE's withholding registration and withholding payment vouchers. For export activities, the WFOE must also complete the import/export enterprise customs registration with China Customs, receiving a ten-digit Customs Registration Code linked to the USCC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC tax system does not provide a check-the-box elective classification or hybrid entity election for a PRC-incorporated WFOE. The WFOE is mandatorily taxed as a resident limited liability enterprise under the Enterprise Income Tax Law; partnership pass-through and disregarded entity status are unavailable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) imposed under the Value-Added Tax Law of the People's Republic of China and administered by the State Taxation Administration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The PRC requires tax registration for every incorporated enterprise regardless of turnover; the statutory economic turnover threshold that triggers mandatory general VAT taxpayer status (as opposed to simplified small-scale taxpayer treatment) is RMB 5,000,000 (CNY 5 million) in annual taxable sales for wholesale enterprises. The WFOE's cement clinker wholesale and exporting activity is expected to exceed this threshold, requiring general VAT taxpayer registration and application of the standard VAT rate on domestic taxable supplies while export sales are zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory use of fully digitalized electronic invoices (Digital E-Invoices) issued through the STA National Electronic Invoice Service Platform or provincial E-Tax Bureau interfaces. VAT invoices must contain the national uniform invoice format, the seller and buyer Unified Social Credit Codes, and an STA-issued tax control code; invoice issuance data is transmitted in real time to the STA for cross-verification with China Customs export declarations. High-volume taxpayers may integrate through system-to-system/API channels. Paper invoices remain permitted only where digitally authorized but must be produced through an STA tax-control UKey and reported to the STA. Anti-fraud validation is performed through the national VAT invoice inspection and digital tax-control stamping system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under PRC VAT law, goods physically exported from China by a resident general VAT taxpayer are zero-rated when sold to an overseas buyer and leave PRC customs territory under customs supervision. The WFOE will not charge the 13% output VAT on the export sale of bulk Portland cement clinker to Taiwan and may claim a refund of creditable input VAT attributable to that export. The zero-rating claim is substantiated by the statutory customs export declaration, ocean bill of lading evidencing carriage from a PRC port to Taiwan, commercial documentation, and collection of export proceeds from the Taiwan buyer via the WFOE's settlement bank. Qualifying offshore digital services are outside the business scope; only the goods leg qualifies for zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Goods Customs Declaration approved by China Customs, bearing the customs declaration number, commercial invoice values, description of goods as Portland cement clinker, and port of export
Ocean or port-to-port Bill of Lading issued by the carrier evidencing shipment from the PRC export port to the Taiwan discharge port
Commercial invoice, packing list, and export sales contract between CN_WFOE_LTD and the Taiwan buyer
Bank foreign exchange receipt record or export proceeds collection note showing receipt of payment through SWIFT LC or TT wire transfer from Taiwan
Export VAT refund/exemption electronic declaration filed through the E-Tax Bureau STA export rebate module linked to the customs export declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and China Customs jointly cross-match export declarations, export VAT refund claims, logistics data, and the 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation record. If the zero-rated export lacks required documentation, fails to evidence actual export, misses the FX repatriation deadline, or is found fraudulent, the STA will claw back the VAT refund or zero-rating benefit, charge late payment surcharge from the refund date, and impose administrative penalties from 50% to 500% of the tax involved. Deliberate misdeclaration or counterfeit documentation triggers criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refund under the PRC Criminal Law, punishable by imprisonment up to life imprisonment and confiscation of property.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC), Foreign Exchange Department; for the mainland China outbound leg, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China is the co-regulator.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Taiwan Dollar is fully convertible for trade and current account transactions, subject to a foreign-exchange declaration through an Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank for each remittance above US$500,000. Capital account transactions, including direct equity investment, inter-company loans, and profit repatriation, are convertible but subject to CBC monitoring and documentation; for a mainland-China parent, the Taiwan leg additionally requires prior approval from the Investment Commission, MOEA. There is no surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds, and exporters may retain and operate foreign-currency deposit accounts freely. Profit remittance from the Taiwan subsidiary requires audited financial statements, board and shareholder resolutions, tax clearance, and a valid foreign-exchange declaration proving the original inward investment. Practical hurdles are not convertibility itself but documentary complexity: banks demand the MOEA approval letter, a credible source-of-wealth file, and a clear capital verification trail before executing any significant cross-border payment. TWD liquidity is deep in onshore money markets, but banks will monitor same-day mega wires for AML and impose intraday limits until the account relationship matures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan imposes no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters must collect foreign currency through an Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank, file a Foreign Exchange Declaration (Form EX) for each transaction, and retain underlying trade documentation, including commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and customs export declaration, for verification. The proceeds may remain 100 percent in a foreign-currency deposit account or be converted to TWD at the discretion of the exporter; no forced conversion timeline applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, Airwallex, and similar non-bank payment providers are legally barred from servicing corporate entities in Taiwan as primary multi-currency accounts because the Taiwan Banking Act limits deposit-taking and foreign-exchange business to licensed banks. There is no EMI passporting regime in Taiwan; a non-bank company accepting customer deposits or executing payments without a banking license commits a regulatory offense. Only FSC-licensed digital banks (LINE Bank, Rakuten International Commercial Bank, Next Commercial Bank) can offer limited digital onboarding, but they still must comply with the same CBC foreign-exchange declaration and capital controls, and none currently provides the full suite of commercial LC, capital escrow, and cross-strait RMB settlement required for a bulk-cement wholesale treasury operation. Therefore, offshore EMIs should be used only for marginal travel or payroll expenses, never as the primary clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a mainland-China-invested Taiwan WFOE, physical in-branch interview is effectively mandatory for the Taiwan statutory representative, normally the general manager or a local director, and for at least one authorized bank signatory. The mainland ultimate beneficial owner or its senior officer should also appear personally at the initial onboarding meeting; some tier-1 banks will accept a notarized power of attorney plus a video interview for the UBO only if the Taiwan director is physically present with the original company chop and corporate seal. Remote consular proxy opening through Taipei Economic and Cultural Office channels is not generally accepted for a mainland investor because the bank cannot adequately verify mainland corporate chops, shareholder resolutions, and the authenticity of notarized signatures without physical inspection. Assume physical presence is mandatory, with a backup requirement for original notarized and certified company documents from mainland China.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identification gap for a mainland-China owner; the ownership chain may terminate at an opaque Hong Kong holding vehicle or a Chinese state-owned enterprise without clear natural-person disclosure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete ownership chart to natural persons; notarized and legalized copies of the Chinese business license, articles of association, shareholder register, and board minutes; audited financial statements of the parent for the last three years; UBO declaration under Taiwan AML rules; certificate of incorporation and register of directors for each intermediate holding; source-of-wealth statements from the remitting bank; and a board resolution confirming the Taiwan entity is a directly held WFOE.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence or delay of MOEA Investment Commission approval for mainland capital; the inbound remittance arrives before the investment permission is finalized or with a non-matching foreign-exchange purpose code.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the final approval letter from the Investment Commission, MOEA; the SAFE and NDRC outbound investment registration certificates from mainland China; the signed equity subscription agreement; a pre-remittance bank reference from the parent's bank; the CBC foreign-exchange declaration form showing purpose code Direct Investment - Equity Contribution; and a CPA capital verification report issued immediately after receipt. The bank will hold funds unallocated until all approvals are stamped and match the exact investment amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade mismatch or commodities sanctions red flags because bulk portland clinker can be transported through multiple vessel operators, transshipment hubs, and intermediaries, creating doubt about whether the cargo is subject to export controls or diverted to a sanctioned end-user.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the full trade chain: HS 2523.10 customs classification, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, vessel IMO numbers, loading-port certificates, independent inspection certificates from SGS or CIQ, purchase agreements, and end-user/end-use statements from each buyer. Provide adverse-media and sanctions screening reports for all directors, UBOs, counterparties, and vessels using commercial databases such as Dow Jones, Refinitiv, LexisNexis, and OFAC lists. Confirm the entity is not dealing with listed parties and that all contract counterparties are pre-vetted before the first LC or TT payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party liquidity flows obscuring true commercial purpose; account activity may be dominated by intercompany funding from the mainland parent, creating concern about round-tripping, disguised capital flight, or transfer-pricing manipulation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a full set of underlying sales contracts with third-party customers, warehouse and logistics contracts, transfer-pricing documentation prepared under Taiwan income-tax rules, audited financial statements, and a rolling cash-flow forecast. Provide bank statements of the Taiwan entity showing actual third-party trade receivables and inventory purchases, not merely parent funding. Substantiate arm's-length pricing with a benchmark report and a letter from a Taiwan tax advisor confirming that related-party transactions are priced and reported consistently with the entities substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Before any wire, the mainland parent must complete NDRC and SAFE outbound investment registrations and obtain a Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate for Outbound Investment. The Taiwan entity must hold an Investment Commission (MOEA) approval letter naming the exact capital amount and the permissible paid-in capital schedule. The parent then instructs its bank to remit via SWIFT MT103 to the beneficiary Capital Escrow Account at an Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank in Taiwan, with the beneficiary account title matching the approved investment and the CBC remittance purpose code Direct Investment - Equity Contribution. The receiving bank will generate an Inward Remittance Notification and a Foreign Exchange Declaration form on behalf of the Taiwan entity. After funds are received, a Taiwan CPA issues a capital verification report confirming paid-in capital, and the entity files the capital increase with the central company registry. No offsetting, netting, or same-day intra-group movement of funds should be executed while the capital is pending verification, and the remittance must be for the exact approved amount to avoid rejection or freezing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for small or urgent TT settlements for bulk cement and clinker purchases; use irrevocable commercial letters of credit under UCP600 for large shipments where title documents and vessel-loading evidence are critical; and use documentary collections (DP/DA) for medium-risk counterparties with established payment history. For cross-strait RMB settlement, payments can be cleared through the RMB clearing mechanism operated by Bank of China Taipei Branch, while USD and TWD settlement continue through SWIFT. Every disbursement must be supported by the commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, inspection or weight certificate, and a true trade-purpose code; the bank will screen the beneficiary, vessel, and underlying transaction against sanctions lists before release of funds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forward contracts for USD/TWD and RMB/TWD with genuine trade or investment exposure and tenors matched to projected cash flows
Cross-currency swaps between TWD and USD for long-term capital and profit-remittance hedging, provided the underlying exposure is documented and approved by the CBC-authorized bank
Plain vanilla FX options on USD/TWD and RMB/TWD for hedging forecasted trade flows, subject to real-exposure verification
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on offshore currencies other than TWD, such as USD/CNY, for mainland China trade exposures; onshore TWD NDFs are not permitted as a domestic retail hedging instrument

FX hedging instruments are permitted only when paired with underlying trade, equity, or dividend flows; speculative or naked derivative positions are prohibited under CBC practice and internal bank suitability policies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year companies: 1 May to 31 May of the following tax year; an electronic return extension may move the return component to 30 June, but the full tax payment remains due by 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 1% of the unpaid tax for each two-day period of delay, capped at 15%; interest at the postal savings annual rate on the unpaid principal; fraudulent understatement subject to a penalty up to three times the evaded tax; if no return is filed and no business activity is shown for six consecutive months, the Ministry of Economic Affairs may administratively dissolve the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and Approved Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting; records held at the registered office and produced to the Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration Office upon inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); the meeting records must be completed and minuted contemporaneously
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The responsible person is liable for fines of New Taiwan dollars 10,000 to 100,000 for failure to convene within the statutory window; repeated non-compliance after MOE notice may support an administrative strike-off order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified Audited Financial Statements and CPA Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Company and Commerce Registration Department; copy to the National Taxation Bureau when the audit threshold is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end) for companies with paid-in capital exceeding TWD 30 million; non-threshold companies retain board-approved statements and need not file a certified pack
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a compulsory CPA-audited pack may result in fines of TWD 10,000 to 50,000 against the responsible person, escalating daily notice penalties, and eventual administrative dissolution by MOE for continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Review and Event-Driven Transparency Platform Notifications
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration and Transparency Platform (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual internal review of the beneficial ownership records must be completed before the annual general meeting, in all cases no later than 30 June; any share transfer or change of responsible person must be filed to the MOE platform within 15 calendar days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted event-driven filing exposes the responsible person to administrative fines of TWD 10,000 to 50,000 per violation; knowingly false filings can lead to higher AML sanctions and administrative dissolution if corrective notices are ignored

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified public accountant audit is statutorily compulsory for a Taiwan-incorporated company if: (i) it is a public company or files financial information with TWSE/TPEx; (ii) it is a non-public company whose paid-in capital at the close of the fiscal year exceeds TWD 30 million (approximately USD 930,000); (iii) it is a regulated financial institution, securities firm, insurer, or money-service business, regardless of the capital threshold; or (iv) it is specifically designated by the National Taxation Bureau or MOE, including revenue-test designations that require a CPA-attested income tax return pack (annual turnover above TWD 100 million). Below these thresholds a WFOE is not required by law to appoint a CPA auditor, but audited financial statements may still be required by shareholders, a foreign parent, or bank documentary credit covenants.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-endorsed International Financial Reporting Standards (T-IFRS) for public companies; non-public companies may elect T-IFRS or apply the Enterprise Accounting Standards (Taiwan SME/GAAP) issued under the Business Entity Accounting Act; financial statements are denominated in New Taiwan dollars and must comply with Income Tax Act and MOE presentation rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the company must at all times keep a current register of every natural or legal person who directly or indirectly controls more than 10% of the paid-in capital or voting shares. Any event-based change in such major shareholder or responsible person must be reported to the MOE Company Registration and Transparency Platform within 15 calendar days. In addition, before each annual general meeting (normally by 30 June), management must perform a full annual reconfirmation of the beneficial ownership chain, log findings in the corporate minute book, and be prepared to demonstrate the trace to the MOE, tax bureau, or bank AML officer on demand.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The PRC WFOE is subject to the standard 25% Corporate Income Tax (CIT) rate. Qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises may use a 15% reduced rate. Small low-profit enterprises may apply a 20% reduced statutory rate, producing an effective rate of approximately 5% on taxable income up to RMB 3 million within the applicable effective window. Qualified R&D expenditure may carry a 100% additional super-deduction. A wholesale distribution and ocean-freight WFOE in the cement sector will not generally obtain a statutory tax holiday unless it is located in a designated encouraged region or otherwise qualifies for an industry-specific incentive.
